subject: Maelstrom9b elevated 5xx/timeouts — mitigation timeline & rollback proposal
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@twinleaf.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Maelstrom9b elevated 5xx/timeouts — mitigation timeline & rollback proposal

Hi Anya —

We observed a sustained increase in 5xx and timeout responses (primarily 504s) from the maelstrom9b model serving pool in us-west-2 starting around 08:40 PDT. Early analysis shows failures concentrated on long-context streaming requests (>=6k tokens) and a correlation with a kernel dispatch change we rolled out yesterday for improved attention performance.

Impact: TwinLeaf reports degraded response rates for select customers (some requests returning 504 after 30s). We've flagged any requests to your production routes and are prioritizing traffic from your account.

Immediate actions we are taking (next 90 minutes):
- Route affected traffic to maelstrom9b-v1-stable (compatible fallback) for your account to restore availability.
- Apply a soft client-side rate cap to streaming sessions where latency > 10s.
- Enable increased autoscale headroom for the dedicated pool serving your requests.
- Collect and preserve logs/traces for audit — attached is an error log excerpt and the rollback playbook we will use if needed.

Proposed next steps for the full remediation:
1) If mitigations hold, we'll perform a controlled rollback of the kernel change to the previous compiled kernel (estimated 3–6 hours) and validate on a canary set of flows.
2) If rollback is not sufficient, we will redirect your traffic to a quantized variant we validated for long-context workloads (estimated 6–12 hours).

We realize the impact here and want to minimize disruption. Please confirm whether you prefer we schedule the full rollback during your low-traffic window (we see 02:00–05:00 PDT) or proceed immediately once canary checks pass.

Attachment: maelstrom9b_error_log_excerpt.txt, rollback_playbook.pdf

Apologies for the disruption — I will provide progress updates approximately every 2 hours until we reach steady state.

— Mateo

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Maelstrom9b elevated 5xx/timeouts — mitigation timeline & rollback proposal

Folks — quick ops note and suggested plan based on triage: we believe root cause is a regression in kernel dispatch selection introduced in the 20270619 kernel rollout. Under long-context streaming workloads the new dispatch path is causing incremental memory fragmentation and premature KV-cache eviction which results in stalled token generation and timeouts (not a hard crash; rather progressive performance collapse).

What we've confirmed so far:
- Error traces show increased "dispatch_wait" metrics and higher per-process RSS variance on nodes running the new kernel.
- The issue reproduces on a synthetic long-context load generator we spun up against a canary cluster.

Immediate mitigation (now):
- Disable the new dispatch flag (flag: enable_kernel_v2_dispatch=false) in the runtime for canary nodes — this reduces the fragmentation behavior and restores steady token service for long contexts.
- For affected pools, set fallback to compiled kernel v1 (manual routing rule) for customers with high long-context traffic (TwinLeaf is already prioritized).
- Deploy a short-lived cache-eviction job to proactively shrink KV caches every 5 minutes for the next 4 hours.

Owners & ETA:
- Karthik to apply the runtime flag disable and confirm canary stability (ETA 45–90 minutes).
- Stephanie to validate customer canary flows and confirm 95th percentile latency delta (ETA 90–120 minutes after canary is up).
- Ben to monitor pool health and coordinate rollback if flag change doesn't stabilize (on-call).

If the canary looks good we should proceed with a wider rollback of the kernel change across the us-west-2 fleet (rolling across AZs to avoid a blast radius). That wider rollback is an estimated 3–6 hour operation with validation steps.

I'll attach the quick triage logs to the incident ticket (INF-7219).

— Ben

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Maelstrom9b elevated 5xx/timeouts — resolution & next steps

Hi Anya —

Update: we rolled the kernel dispatch change back on the affected us-west-2 nodes after successful canary validation. Timeline: initial mitigations (routing to v1-stable + runtime flag disable) applied within 60 minutes of detection on Jun 20; canary validation completed on Jun 21; full rollback completed by 15:30 PDT on Jun 22.

Outcome: 5xx and timeout rates for TwinLeaf production routes returned to baseline within ~40 minutes of the rollback. Stephanie has the latency graphs attached in the incident ticket; Ben's team will continue elevated monitoring for 48 hours.

What we preserved/provided per your request:
- All request-level logs for TwinLeaf have been archived to the shared Drive folder and retained for 30 days. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/maelstrom9b/rca-20270622
- Final RCA (summary): root cause = kernel dispatch regression causing KV-cache fragmentation under long-context streaming; corrective change = rollback + additional regression tests for long-context token streaming in our CI.

Next steps for follow-up (owners):
- Infra (Karthik): permanent fix and improved telemetry to detect fragmentation earlier (ETA: two sprints).
- Runtime (Ben): harden canary tests and add a guardrail to avoid auto-rollouts without long-context load validation (ETA: next sprint).
- Customer success (Rachel): coordinate compensation/credits for impacted usage with TwinLeaf (Rachel will follow up).

We regret the impact and appreciate your patience while we restored service. If you'd like, we can schedule a short post-incident review with your team and our infra/runtime leads to walk through the RCA.

Best,
— Mateo
